changes.title: Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on now supports custom OpenTelemetry and Prometheus telemetry
changes.detail: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces support for your own application telemetry in the CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on. The CloudWatch agent you already run now accepts metrics, traces, and logs from your applications, so you don't deploy and operate a separate collector to get them into CloudWatch. Applications instrumented with an OpenTelemetry SDK send to an OTLP endpoint that the agent serves on every node, on by default. changes.title: Amazon Transcribe announces a synchronous transcription API
changes.detail: Amazon Transcribe now offers a synchronous transcription API, `TranscribeAudio`. Send a complete audio file in a single request and get the full transcript back in the same response. There is no job to start, no status to poll, no connection to manage. Add fast, accurate speech-to-text to interactive applications such as voice assistants, agent-assist tools and on-demand "transcribe this clip" features. changes.title: Amazon DynamoDB vector search now supports new inline filter operators
changes.detail: Amazon DynamoDB vector search inline filters now support range comparisons, value lists, and logical operators in addition to the equality operator, so you can narrow a vector search to exactly the items you want. You can now filter on numeric ranges such as price, rating, or publish date, match an attribute against a list of values, check whether an attribute exists, and combine conditions with OR and NOT. changes.title: Amazon S3 Vectors raises the filterable metadata limit to 40 KB per vector
changes.detail: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports up to 40 KB of filterable metadata per vector, up from 2 KB. You can attach and filter on more attributes per vector, such as category, permissions, timestamps, and descriptive tags, so your retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic, and semantic-search applications can narrow results by more of the fields that matter to them. S3 Vectors provides native support to store and query vectors in Amazon S3, delivering purpose-built, cost-optimized vector storage and query at billion-vector scale. changes.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 7 additional AWS regions
changes.detail: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 7 additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Canada (Central), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), South America (São Paulo), and US West (N. California). With this launch, you can use Lambda MicroVMs in a total of 21 AWS Regions. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume speeds, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code. changes.title: AgentCore runtime instances now support Amazon EC2 G7 instances
changes.detail: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances now support Amazon EC2 G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. G7 instances give agents that do 3D rendering or model inference another GPU option, alongside families such as G6e and G7e. changes.title: Amazon Transcribe now available in AWS European Sovereign Cloud
changes.detail: Amazon Transcribe is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. Customers who need to keep data and operations within the EU for regulatory compliance and data sovereignty requirements can now use automatic speech recognition (ASR) in the Region to turn speech into text. Amazon Transcribe offers two ways to transcribe audio in this Region. Batch transcription processes media files stored in Amazon S3, and streaming transcription returns text in real time from live audio over HTTP/2 or WebSocket. changes.title: IAM Roles Anywhere now supports aliases to simplify workload configuration
changes.detail: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles Anywhere now supports aliases, which are readable names that you assign to trust anchors, profiles, and certificate revocation lists (CRLs). Your workloads can request temporary credentials using a trust anchor or profile alias Amazon Resource Name (ARN) instead of an ARN with a system-generated ID, and you can use alias ARNs in many of the operations that manage these resources. Aliases make configurations easier to read and review: an alias ARN that ends in alias/trust-anchor/production-ca can show which certificate authority (CA) a workload use
